Experimental Investigation of Multi-material Deposition Using GMAW-Based WAAM

Abstract:

Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) provides a flexible and scalable approach for the fabrication of metallic components through layer-wise material deposition. The present investigation focuses on the development and experimental evaluation of a Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW)-based WAAM process for copper deposition as the first stage toward copper-based multimaterial and Cu-Al functionally graded structures. The study initially investigates aluminium and copper separately to establish their baseline deposition behaviour and suitable processing conditions. Aluminium deposition is evaluated using a Taguchi experimental design, while copper deposition is investigated using a Central Composite Design to examine the influence of wire feed speed, travel speed and welding voltage on bead formation. Bead width, bead height and penetration characteristics are considered as the primary geometric responses, together with visual assessment of deposition quality and stability. The preliminary results establish the deposition behaviour and an initial processing region for copper under the developed GMAW-based WAAM system. Further microstructural, elemental and phase characterization will be carried out to support the selection of suitable deposition conditions before progressing toward dissimilar Cu-Al deposition and controlled multimaterial fabrication. The present work therefore establishes the experimental foundation for the subsequent development of copper-based alloy and functionally graded WAAM structures.
Keywords: WAAM, GMAW, Bead Geometry, Multimaterial AM, Cu-Al.
